blocks.body: Hydro jetting clears a sewer line with a high-pressure water stream, fed through the same cleanout access point used for rodding. A specialized nozzle sprays water in every direction as it moves through the pipe, scouring grease, scale, and roots off the entire pipe wall instead of just cutting a path through the middle. It's the fix for buildup that keeps coming back after rodding, or for roots that have worked into the pipe joints. Rodding opens the line back up. Hydro jetting cleans it.

img.alt: Diagram showing how hydro jetting clears a residential sewer line, with a cross-section view of the underground pipe, jet nozzle, high-pressure water spray, and debris being flushed toward the street connection

tiles.h3: Mineral Scale Has Narrowed the Pipe
tiles.body: Hard groundwater leaves scale inside drain lines over the years. Jetting removes it so the pipe carries its full volume.

tiles.h3: Grease Keeps Clogging the Kitchen Line
tiles.body: Rodding pokes a hole in grease. Jetting strips it off the pipe walls.
Jetting clears fine roots that rodding leaves behind at the joints.
Every lining job starts with a jetted, clean pipe.

blocks.h2: Hydro Jetting and McHenry County Water
blocks.intro: Hydro jetting is a common fix for McHenry County drain lines, and the local water is part of the reason.

items.body: McHenry County gets its water from underground aquifers, and groundwater here tends to be hard. Minerals deposit inside drain lines along with soap and grease, building a crust that rodding can't remove.
Many McHenry homes were built for families in the 1990s and 2000s. Decades of cooking grease in the same kitchen line adds up.
Where a line has settled, water sits and debris builds faster. Jetting cleans it out while you plan the repair.
We confirm the pipe can handle the pressure first and show you the result when we're done.

blocks.h2: What Happens When You Call J. Blanton

steps.body: We check for breaks or a collapse, since jetting a broken pipe can make it worse.
We clean to the main, adjusting pressure for the pipe material.
A second camera pass, and you get the price before any of it starts.

blocks.h2: Hydro Jetting Questions From McHenry Homeowners

items.q: Does hard water really build up in drain pipes?
items.preview: Yes. Minerals combine with soap and grease into scale.
items.answer: Yes. Hard water leaves mineral deposits that bond with soap scum and grease. Over years, that crust narrows the pipe and catches debris. Jetting removes it.

items.q: Is hydro jetting better than snaking?
items.preview: For buildup, yes. For a simple clog, snaking is enough.
items.answer: A snake or rod opens a path through a clog quickly. Jetting cleans the entire pipe wall, which matters when scale, grease or roots keep bringing the clog back.

items.q: Can hydro jetting be used on a septic line?
items.preview: Yes, on the line to the tank, with care.
items.answer: Yes. We can jet the line from the house to the septic tank. We'll avoid sending excess debris into the tank and tell you if the tank needs pumping.

items.q: How long do jetting results last?
items.preview: Often years for grease and scale, with good habits.
items.answer: For grease and scale, often years. Roots grow back over time, so lines with roots usually need a yearly check.

items.q: How much does hydro jetting cost in McHenry?
items.preview: It depends on the line and buildup. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the length of the line, access and how much buildup there is. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
